about: Regression cases for kai review-commit, taken from Martian's Code Review Bench (github.com/withmartian/code-review-benchmark, offline/golden_comments) and Kai's own findings on the 2026-09-24 run (the jschatz1/*__kai__PR*__20260924 forks, PR #1). base/head are the fork's PR #1. 'expect' is a golden comment Kai must publish: a published claim matches when it names the file and contains one of 'any' (case-insensitive). 'forbid' is a finding Kai published and must not: any published claim that names the file and contains one of 'any' fails the case. 'at_most' caps how many published claims may match, for one root cause posted several times. Run with scripts/review-regressions.sh.

expect.golden: retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; use an atomic increment.

forbid.was: New retryCount > 1 deletion branch omits the method: SMS guard; dormant today but will silently delete email/whatsapp reminders if retry-incrementing is ever added to those paths.

expect.golden: backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back; two concurrent logins with the same code can both pass, so a one-time code is accepted more than once.

forbid.was: minLength/maxLength are native constraint attributes, not zod validation.
disable path relies on terminal-wipe for single-use; a future non-terminal step would break the exactly-once invariant. (baseline run 2026-09-25, v0.35.89)

expect.golden: refreshFunction returns the fetch Response in sync mode, but callers such as GoogleCalendarService expect res.data / an integration-specific token.
refreshOAuthTokens is passed credentialId instead of userId, breaking the credential-sync user lookup.
jsforce.Connection is created with the stale credentialKey.access_token/instance_url after a token refresh.

forbid.was: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED holds the encryption-key string, not a boolean; latent footgun for future strict comparisons.
no HTTP method guard and unhandled Zod parse throw; inconsistent with every other handler.

at_most.was: HubSpot, Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM each got their own finding for one refreshOAuthTokens return-shape mismatch.

expect.golden: hasPermission looks the per-client resource up with findByName(server, client.getId(), ...) but getOrCreateResource creates it with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so the lookup never finds it.
getClientsWithPermission returns resource.getName() of the type-level resource, while getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects client IDs for realm.getClientById.

forbid.was: testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient never asserts that an admin with MANAGE_CLIENTS is still allowed.

expect.golden: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes and collects groupResource.getId(), but hasPermission resolves resources by name (a group id) and callers use the result as group IDs.
canManage() falls back to VIEW and MANAGE scopes, so view-only users pass it. (Kai found this on 2026-09-24; keep it.)
The translation is in Italian instead of Lithuanian. (Kai found this on 2026-09-24; keep it.)

forbid.was: this change introduces the host malicious.com, which no file outside the change mentions.
tests assert only that some Illegal HTML message exists.
